examples.question_text: $X\sim\text{Bin}(4,0.4)$. Find $P(X\le1)$, correct to four decimal places.
A player takes five independent shots, each with probability $0.4$ of scoring. Find the probability that she scores at least once, correct to four decimal places.
examples.solution_text:
Let $X$ count the shots scored. Then $X\sim\text{Bin}(5,0.4)$. The complement of at least one success is zero successes.
$\begin{align*}P(X\ge1)&=1-P(X=0)\\&=1-(0.6)^5\\&=1-0.07776\\&\approx0.9222\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: Each component is faulty with probability $0.4$, independently of the others. Five components are tested. Explain whether direct addition or the complement uses fewer terms, then find the probability that at least two are faulty, correct to four decimal places.
examples.solution_text:
Let $X$ count faulty components. Then $X\sim\text{Bin}(5,0.4)$. At least two means $r\in\{2,3,4,5\}$. The complement $\{0,1\}$ uses two terms instead of four.
$\begin{align*}P(X=0)&=(0.6)^5=0.07776\\P(X=1)&={}^{5}C_1(0.4)(0.6)^4=0.2592\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}P(X\ge2)&=1-P(X=0)-P(X=1)\\&=1-0.07776-0.2592\\&\approx0.6630\end{align*}$

examples.question_text:
$X\sim\text{Bin}(5,0.4)$. Find each probability, using whichever set has fewer terms. Give answers correct to four decimal places.
(a) $P(X>1)$
(b) $P(X>3)$
examples.solution_text:
(a) More than one means $r\in\{2,3,4,5\}$. Use the shorter complement $\{0,1\}$.
$\begin{align*}P(X>1)&=1-P(X=0)-P(X=1)\\&=1-(0.6)^5-{}^{5}C_1(0.4)(0.6)^4\\&\approx0.6630\end{align*}$
(b) More than three means $r\in\{4,5\}$. Add these two terms directly; the complement has four terms.
$\begin{align*}P(X>3)&=P(X=4)+P(X=5)\\&={}^{5}C_4(0.4)^4(0.6)+(0.4)^5\\&=0.0768+0.01024\\&\approx0.0870\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: $X\sim\text{Bin}(4,0.4)$. Find $P(X<2)$ and $P(X\le2)$, correct to four decimal places. Explain why they differ.
examples.solution_text:
$X$ is integer-valued. The strict inequality includes only $0,1$; the inclusive inequality also includes $2$.
$\begin{align*}P(X<2)&=P(X=0)+P(X=1)\\&=(0.6)^4+{}^{4}C_1(0.4)(0.6)^3\\&=0.4752\end{align*}$
$P(X=2)={}^{4}C_2(0.4)^2(0.6)^2=0.3456$.
$\begin{align*}P(X\le2)&=P(X<2)+P(X=2)\\&=0.4752+0.3456\\&=0.8208\end{align*}$

examples.derivation: Five independent shots with constant success probability 0.4 give Bin(5,0.4). P(X≥1)=1−0.6^5=1−0.07776=0.92224, rounding to 0.9222.
The direct set contains four outcomes; its complement contains two. P(X=0)=0.07776 and P(X=1)=5(0.4)(0.6^4)=0.2592. P(X≥2)=1−0.07776−0.2592=0.66304, rounding to 0.6630.

(a) X>1 includes 2 through 5; the shorter complement gives 1−0.07776−0.2592=0.66304, or 0.6630. (b) X>3 includes only 4 and 5: 5(0.4^4)(0.6)+0.4^5=0.0768+0.01024=0.08704, or 0.0870. Direct addition uses two terms rather than four.
X<2 includes 0 and 1, giving 0.1296+0.3456=0.4752. P(X=2)=6(0.4^2)(0.6^2)=0.3456. Thus P(X≤2)=0.4752+0.3456=0.8208; the difference is exactly the included boundary probability.
The inclusive interval contains 2 and 3. P(X=2)=10(0.4^2)(0.6^3)=0.3456 and P(X=3)=10(0.4^3)(0.6^2)=0.2304. Their sum is 0.5760.
